tools.title: Figma MCP
tools.description: Figma’s official MCP reads design context and can create or update native frames, components, variables, auto layout, and specs through supported clients and skills.
tools.recommendation: Use it to connect design context with implementation and editable canvas work. The remote server has the broadest feature set; verify generated changes against the actual components and layout.

tools.title: Playwright MCP
tools.description: Lets an AI agent inspect and operate browser interfaces through structured accessibility data for repeatable product checks and walkthroughs.
tools.recommendation: Use it for a small repeatable browser check or flow review, then keep sensitive sessions out of test runs.

tools.title: Apple Design Skill
tools.description: A reusable skill for checking Apple-platform interface work against platform design guidance and implementation conventions.
tools.recommendation: Use it as a platform-specific review lens, then confirm important decisions against current Apple guidance.

tools.title: Emil Kowalski’s skills
tools.description: A compact collection of design-engineering skills focused on motion, interface detail, and more intentional frontend execution.
tools.recommendation: Strong material for raising the quality bar in implementation. Best used selectively, with the team’s own interaction principles layered on top.

tools.title: Scroll Craft
tools.description: A skill for planning and refining scroll-driven experiences, including pacing, transitions, and implementation choices.
tools.recommendation: Try it on one scroll-heavy page concept first, then check reduced motion and performance before shipping.

tools.title: Mobbin MCP
tools.description: Connects AI workflows to Mobbin’s library of real product screens and flows for pattern research and comparison.
tools.recommendation: Use it to compare one key flow against shipped products, then adapt the pattern instead of copying it directly.

tools.title: Savee MCP
tools.description: Searches Savee’s curated reference library and can retrieve personal saves, boards, feed items, and image content in supported clients.
tools.recommendation: Use it to ground one art-direction pass in existing saves, then keep the output distinct from the reference material.

tools.title: ScreensDesign MCP
tools.description: Provides read-only access to real mobile screens, full recordings, paywalls, onboarding, and user flows from a large app library.
tools.recommendation: A useful research layer for flow-level comparison, especially when isolated screenshots hide interaction context. Validate coverage for your market before relying on it.

tools.title: Cosmos
tools.description: A visual discovery and collecting tool for organizing references, exploring related imagery, and building a durable taste library.
tools.recommendation: Useful now because it supports the slow work of collecting and organizing taste, not only generating output. Shared clusters can also make critique references more concrete.

tools.title: Ploy
tools.description: An AI website builder for drafting marketing pages from an existing site and brand system, with reusable sections and components.
tools.recommendation: Interesting for constrained page drafting because it starts from existing brand material. We still need to test how well it preserves hierarchy and system logic at scale.

tools.title: Raylight
tools.description: A motion-design editor for turning product interfaces into polished launch and product videos with AI-assisted canvas edits.
tools.recommendation: Try it on a single product shot or hero video before moving larger motion narratives into production.

tools.title: Geometric
tools.description: A browser-based image and motion art tool for transforming source material through configurable geometric and visual effects.
tools.recommendation: Useful as a deliberate visual detour when a team needs material beyond interface references. Its value is exploration, not automatic brand fit.

tools.title: Canva MCP
tools.description: Canva’s remote MCP now exposes design creation and editing, asset and brand management, library search, export, and commenting through AI assistants.
tools.recommendation: Trial it on one small edit and review loop, then verify permissions and brand library behavior in your workspace.

tools.title: Canva Skills
tools.description: The official Canva skills package adds reusable workflows for resize, bulk create, feedback implementation, and approval-gated edits, bundled for Claude, Cursor, and Codex through the Canva Connector.
tools.recommendation: Start with one supported workflow on a single design, then confirm the output stays consistent with your team library and approvals.

tools.title: Pinterest MCP
tools.description: Pinterest’s announced official MCP is intended to search Pins, explore and manage Boards, follow trends, and surface audience and advertising insights.
tools.recommendation: The official page shows an endpoint and scoped authorization but still invites launch sign-ups. Keep watching until access and personal-board permissions are confirmed in a working account.

tools.title: UI Design Agent Kit
tools.description: A project-level UI agent workflow that turns plain-language briefs into a design contract, implementation plan, browser checks, and recorded delivery evidence.
tools.recommendation: Its explicit design contract and browser evidence are promising. The kit is broad and opinionated, so test one bounded workflow before adopting its full tool routing.

tools.title: Seenry Skills
tools.description: An eight-skill design collection for research, composition, assets, motion, mobile UI, branding, decks, and video. Optional Seenry MCP adds captured-screen evidence.
tools.recommendation: Start with one skill, such as reference research or review, before adopting the full workflow.

tools.title: Dembrandt
tools.description: This MCP and CLI extracts colors, typography, spacing, borders, shadows, motion, components, breakpoints, and WCAG contrast findings from live websites.
tools.recommendation: Run it against a few reference sites to compare tokens and accessibility findings before using them as evidence.

tools.title: Diagram Design
tools.description: A Codex-compatible design skill for producing structured, editable diagrams, including user journeys and flow diagrams.
tools.recommendation: Apply it to one user journey or service flow, then compare the structure and labels against your current documentation.

tools.title: Figma Motion
tools.description: A timeline inside Figma Design for editable keyframe animation, reusable motion styles, and supported Lottie exports. The 30 September release extends its open beta.
tools.recommendation: Test one component animation and its exported result before moving a motion system. Reusable styles could reduce repeated setup; beta behavior and export fidelity still need a team trial.

tools.title: Framer Skills
tools.description: Project-level instructions for the Framer agent covering design systems, writing style, and CMS workflows. Skills can reference project pages, components, and styles and travel with a remix.
tools.recommendation: Capture one agreed rule in a Framer project and test whether it is applied consistently on a second page.

tools.title: Iconiq UI
tools.description: An open-source UI collection delivered as editable local components through the shadcn registry, with an optional connection through shadcn MCP.
tools.recommendation: A team-submitted lead for restrained component motion. Check keyboard behavior, reduced motion, and design-system fit in a small prototype before recommending it for product work.

tools.title: Figma agent
tools.description: In Figma Design, the agent can connect a library from the file, reference specific components, variables, and styles with @, and use that context to produce outputs aligned to the team system.
tools.setup: Open Agents in a Figma Design file
tools.recommendation: Use it for one bounded edit on a file with an existing library, then check component reuse and hierarchy before wider adoption.

tools.title: Scenario Agent Skills
tools.description: A set of agent skills for producing images, video, audio, textures, skyboxes, and 3D assets through the Scenario MCP, with separate expert tools for Blender, Maya, ZBrush, Unreal, and Unity.
tools.recommendation: Use it for one small branded asset task, such as a single image or 3D concept, before expanding to a wider production workflow.
tools.setup: Not stated; check whether the MCP or local DCC tool path fits your workflow

tools.title: agent-skills
tools.description: The skill builds a UI from a design spec, renders it, audits accessibility, and fixes mismatches, with explicit verification in its workflow.
tools.recommendation: Try it on one design-spec-to-UI loop, then compare the rendered result with the original spec and accessibility requirements.
tools.setup: Plugin or skills CLI; host specific

tools.title: Design-components-for-AI-agents
tools.description: The repository provides animated React, Tailwind CSS, and React Native components, plus design briefs and JSON prompts, with examples that include motion, charts, navigation, and other UI patterns.
tools.recommendation: Use one component as a starting point for a single screen or interaction, then verify it fits your stack and motion rules.
tools.setup: Project install or registry setup; host details vary

tools.title: OpenDesign
tools.description: A collaborative AI design workspace where teams start from a brief, create prototypes with an agent, share feedback, and refine in the same project.
tools.recommendation: Source-reviewed; not yet team-tested. Pilot it on one team prototype loop and confirm the workflow fits your review and handoff process before adopting it broadly.
tools.setup: Not stated; local-first workspace and cloud options are mentioned

tools.title: chudarin-design-skills
tools.description: The skill set is built for Figma work from components and variables, including planning flows, building screens, finding design system debt, fixing bindings, and making presentations.
tools.recommendation: Use it on one Figma file with existing components and variables, then check whether binding fixes and screen edits stay targeted.
tools.setup: Not stated; plugin and Figma file access are implied

tools.title: Framesmith uses a visual canvas and quality gate for UI design
tools.description: This open-source MCP server turns an AI coding agent into a UI designer with a visual canvas, vetted design patterns, and a quality gate before designs are shown.
tools.recommendation: Source-reviewed; not yet team-tested. Try it on one design iteration that needs a quality gate, then compare the canvas output with your current review criteria.
tools.setup: Not stated; MCP client setup required

tools.title: REA can inspect app behavior and explain it with evidence
tools.description: REA connects agents to local analysis tools for binaries, apps, and websites, and returns evidence and limitations so the agent can explain how a feature works and build from it.
tools.recommendation: Source-reviewed; not yet team-tested. Use it for one feature investigation where you need evidence-backed reverse engineering, then confirm the findings against the actual product behavior.
tools.setup: npx rea-agents setup or official release path

tools.title: RasanAI is a guided video direction skill with staged approvals
tools.description: The skill directs launch films and motion graphics through a staged flow with brief, story, look, animatic, and final review steps in a browser console.
tools.recommendation: Source-reviewed; not yet team-tested. Try it on one short launch film brief first, then validate the story, look, and timing before a larger motion project.
tools.access: Claude Code and optional Mac app
tools.setup: Not stated; agent skill works without the Mac app

findings.title: Figma agent
findings.summary: Generally available since 6 October, with library guidelines, file search, and custom skills. It now uses AI credits. Test one library-backed edit and inspect the result before adopting it.
